name: Washington, DC
summary: The nation's capital — the monuments, the free Smithsonians, the Capitol, and Arlington — and the close of the East Coast leg. Plan on a full week-plus.

lodging.name: A hotel near the National Mall or Dupont Circle
lodging.blurb: Mall-adjacent for the monuments; Dupont/Logan for dining and nightlife.

foodMustTry.name: A half-smoke at Ben's Chili Bowl
foodMustTry.blurb: A U Street institution since 1958 — the city's signature sausage.

days.label: Day 137 — The National Mall & Monuments
days.summary: Walk the length of the Mall, memorial to memorial. (Mount Vernon is a short drive back into the city.)

item.title: Monuments walk: Lincoln, WWII, Vietnam, Korean, MLK

location.name: Lincoln Memorial
location.address: 2 Lincoln Memorial Cir NW, Washington, DC

item.blurb: From the Lincoln Memorial and its reflecting pool past the WWII, Vietnam, Korean, and MLK memorials to the Washington Monument.

days.label: Day 138 — Smithsonian I
days.summary: Two of the great free museums on the Mall.

item.title: National Air & Space Museum
item.blurb: The Wright Flyer, the Apollo 11 command module, and Lindbergh's Spirit of St. Louis — free.

item.title: National Museum of Natural History

location.name: National Museum of Natural History
location.address: 10th St & Constitution Ave NW, Washington, DC

item.blurb: The Hope Diamond, the dinosaur hall, and the giant elephant in the rotunda.

days.label: Day 139 — Smithsonian II
days.summary: American history and the museum everyone wants to see.

item.title: National Museum of African American History & Culture
item.blurb: The Smithsonian's most sought-after museum — start in the history galleries below ground and work up. Free timed passes recommended.

item.title: National Museum of American History
item.blurb: The original Star-Spangled Banner, the First Ladies' gowns, and Americana.

days.label: Day 140 — Capitol Hill
days.summary: The seat of government and the founding documents.

item.title: U.S. Capitol & Library of Congress
item.blurb: Tour the Rotunda and Statuary Hall (book ahead), then the breathtaking Library of Congress and the Supreme Court across the street.

item.title: The National Archives
item.blurb: See the original Declaration of Independence, Constitution, and Bill of Rights.

days.label: Day 141 — The White House & Ford's Theatre
days.summary: The people's house and a night in 1865.

item.title: The White House & Lafayette Square
item.blurb: View the executive mansion from the fence (tours require advance request through your representative), plus the Ellipse and Lafayette Square.

item.title: Ford's Theatre
item.blurb: Where Lincoln was assassinated, with the museum and the Petersen House where he died across the street.

days.label: Day 142 — Free Day
days.summary: So many museums, so pick a favorite — or just rest. Options below.

freeMenu.title: National Gallery of Art
freeMenu.blurb: The only Leonardo in the Americas, plus a vast free collection and a sculpture garden.

freeMenu.title: International Spy Museum
freeMenu.blurb: Real tradecraft, gadgets, and Cold War history.

freeMenu.title: Smithsonian National Zoo
freeMenu.blurb: Free, and home to giant pandas.

days.label: Day 143 — Arlington
days.summary: A somber morning across the river.

item.title: Arlington National Cemetery
item.blurb: The changing of the guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, JFK's eternal flame, and the Marine Corps (Iwo Jima) Memorial nearby.

days.label: Day 144 — Georgetown & the Tidal Basin
days.summary: A gentler last day in the capital.

item.title: Tidal Basin: Jefferson & FDR Memorials

location.name: Jefferson Memorial
location.address: 16 E Basin Dr SW, Washington, DC

item.blurb: A loop around the water past the Jefferson, FDR, and MLK memorials (cherry blossoms if the timing ever lands here in spring).

item.title: Georgetown & Ben's Chili Bowl
item.blurb: Cobblestone shopping along the C&O Canal, then a half-smoke at Ben's Chili Bowl on U Street.

days.label: Day 145 — South into Virginia
days.summary: Leave the capital and turn south — the East Coast leg is done.

commute.scenicNote: West and south into the Blue Ridge as the trip turns toward the Carolinas.
